hero.alt: Daymark Today screen: Good morning, the next event (Dentist at 11:00 AM), and today’s rituals.
hero.caption: Today

chapters.title: Plan the day.
chapters.intro: Today puts the next event first, then your tasks and rituals. Add a task or check in on a ritual without opening another page.

steps.alt: Today’s brief: next up, Dentist at 11:00 AM; four tasks open and one done; seven of ten rituals kept; 100 minutes of focus; and an Ask Daymark button.
steps.title: A brief, when you want one.
steps.body: Tap Brief for what is next, what is open, the rituals kept, and today’s focus, with Ask Daymark one tap away.
steps.caption: Today’s brief

steps.alt: Event details for Dentist: today from 11:00 to 11:45 AM at Market Street, the forecast for that hour, and an Edit event button.
steps.title: Everything about the next event.
steps.body: Open an event for its time, place, calendar, and the forecast for that hour. Get directions, duplicate, share, or edit it from the same sheet.
steps.caption: Event details

steps.alt: Day view for Friday, November 27: the week strip above hourly events from the morning walk to lunch with Sam.
steps.title: See the day in hours.
steps.body: Open the day to see events laid out in time, and step through the week from the strip above.
steps.caption: Day

steps.alt: Today layout settings: Next up, Rituals, Weather, Tasks, and Day, each with a switch and a drag handle.
steps.title: Choose what Today shows.
steps.body: Turn sections on or off and drag them into the order you want. The greeting stays at the top.
steps.caption: Today layout

chapters.title: Keep a practice.
chapters.intro: Set a daily, weekday, or weekly rhythm, then review check-ins across the week.

steps.alt: Rituals page for today: seven of nine kept, with streaks, and a switch between Today, Week, and History.
steps.title: Check in across the week.
steps.body: Use daily, weekday, or weekly cadences. Check in from Today or the Rituals page, and look across the week or the history.
steps.caption: Rituals

chapters.title: Protect your attention.
chapters.intro: Give one task a protected block of time, then see where today’s focus went.

steps.alt: Focus page with a 25-minute dial, a Begin focus button, and 25, 50, and 90 minute lengths.
steps.title: One dial, one task.
steps.body: Run a Pomodoro with focus, short rest, and long rest, or pick a 25, 50, or 90 minute session.
steps.caption: Focus

chapters.title: Review what mattered.
chapters.intro: Review gathers the week’s finished tasks, focus sessions, and ritual check-ins as they happen.

steps.alt: Review for November 23 to 29: one task done, 350 focus minutes, five days marked, ritual counts so far, and the week’s prompts.
steps.title: A week you can see.
steps.body: Tasks done, focus minutes, and rituals kept so far sit above three prompts: what mattered, what got in the way, and one change for next week.
steps.caption: Review

chapters.title: Save what you want to find again.
chapters.intro: Notes, links, and images in one place. Share from another app and it lands on the Shelf the next time you open Daymark.

steps.alt: Shelf with ten entries, three pinned, a search field, filters for notes, links, and images, and a pinned photo.
steps.title: Filter by kind or tag.
steps.body: Pin what should stay on top, and tag entries so they are easy to gather again.
steps.caption: Shelf

steps.alt: Search for “walk” finding the Morning walk event and the Morning walk ritual.
steps.title: Find anything in the daybook.
steps.body: Search tasks, events, Shelf entries, rituals, and weekly reviews from one field. Spotlight indexing is optional.
steps.caption: Search

chapters.title: Ask about your day.
chapters.intro: Ask Daymark answers from your daybook and makes typed, explainable changes. It works offline, with or without the optional model.

steps.alt: Ask Daymark on iPhone turning “I need to remember to water the plants” into a task for today, with an Undo receipt.
steps.title: From a sentence to a task.
steps.body: Typed commands such as “remember to” or “add a task” make the change directly and show a receipt with Undo. No model is needed.
steps.caption: Typed command · iPhone

steps.alt: Ask Daymark on iPhone with Gemma 4 Fast answering “What should I do first today?” from the day’s tasks.
steps.title: Answers from your daybook.
steps.body: With the optional Gemma 4 model, Daybook mode answers questions from your own tasks and events, on the device.
steps.caption: Gemma 4 Fast · iPhone

steps.alt: Ask Daymark in Open chat with the Fast model installed, two suggestions, and a Web control.
steps.title: Open conversation, on request.
steps.body: Switch to Open chat for general questions. Web search is off unless you turn it on.
steps.caption: Open chat

chapters.title: Yours to set.
chapters.intro: Daymark starts empty and stays quiet until you ask for more.

steps.alt: Look and feel settings: System, Daylight, and paper choices, accent color, Next up pattern, and haptics.
steps.title: Choose the paper.
steps.body: Pick a paper tone and an accent, or let Daylight move the page with the sun.
steps.caption: Appearance

steps.alt: Calendar and Reminders settings with calendar access off and a Connect button.
steps.title: Your calendar, live.
steps.body: Connect Apple Calendar and Reminders, then choose the calendars and lists Daymark reads. Edits save back to those accounts.
steps.caption: Calendar & Reminders
